title: Shalom! Reading direction
topic: reading right to left; ש ל מ ם; the vowels a and o
why: Your very first Hebrew lesson: we set up the reading direction, how vowels (niqqud) work, and five letters, along with the essential greetings.

{"lessons": ["

We read from right to left

Hebrew is written and read from right to left. There are no capital or lowercase letters, and the alphabet, the alef-bet, has only consonants: 22 letters.

The vowels are small marks, dots and dashes, placed under or above the letters: the niqqud. Children's books and textbooks use it; newspapers and street signs almost never do. To start with, you'll always have the vowels.

שָׁלוֹםshalom: hello, goodbye, peace

The right reflex: always start with the letter furthest to the right.

", "

Your first five letters

LetterNameSound
שׁshinsh (dot at the top right)
לlamedl
מmemm
םfinal memm, at the end of a word
הhelight h, silent at the end of a word
וֹvav + doto

Five letters have a special form at the end of a word. The first one: מ becomes ם, as in שָׁלוֹם and שָׁם (there).

The trap: ה at the end of a word is not pronounced. מָה is read simply \"ma\".

", "

The vowels a and o

MarkSoundExample
מָ / מַ (a dash or a small T under the letter)a (as in father)מָה ma
לוֹ (dot on the vav)o (as in more)לוֹ lo

The vowel is read after the letter that carries it: מָ = ma. Then you put the syllables together:

שָׁ + לוֹ + םsha + lo + m = shalom

To ask how someone is: מָה שְׁלוֹמְךָ? to a man, מָה שְׁלוֹמֵךְ? to a woman. Hebrew always distinguishes between a masculine \"you\" and a feminine \"you\". The answer is טוֹב, תּוֹדָה: fine, thanks.
